page: Amazon Web Services t3.large is a burstable performance instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance provides 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 4.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the t3.large operates in the lower performance tiers. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance is categorized as weak, while multi-core CPU performance falls into the poor category. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 93.13 GB/sec, but this drops to 12.87 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Geekbench metrics, including single-core and multi-core scores, consistently rank in the bottom 10%. Similarly, database operations and Redis SET operations reflect low-tier performance characteristics.

The burstable CPU allocation model of the t3.large offers a qualitative cost-efficiency advantage for workloads with variable CPU utilization. By utilizing a CPU credit system, it provides a low-cost entry point for applications that remain idle or run at low baseline levels but require occasional bursts of compute power. However, the poor performance in sustained multi-core benchmarks, software compilation, and LLM inference tasks makes it unsuitable for continuous high-load processing. Appropriate workloads include low-traffic web servers, small development or test environments, code repositories, and light background scripting tasks.
